newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends firm, follows lead of crude, swap.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends firm, follows lead of crude, swap.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended modestly higher on Thursday as Brent crude and swaps overshadowed what was seen as a balanced market.

Traders said the physical market was quiet and reluctantly moved higher, but it would continue to stairstep higher as long as crude was strong and the concentrated buying in the swaps market continued.
"Based on naphtha as an island, the market is fairly well balanced," said one trader. "I think it's more a function of distillates and the crude dragging naphtha around."
Buying interest for pipeline spec material for delivery by Nov 25 was seen in the market but traders said there was not a clear bidding price.
Another source said two Alexandria cargoes were likely to become available in the second half of November as well as two to three Skikda cargoes.
Bids were being re-entered for Egypt's 1997 tender and results now were not expected until next week.
Rumours this week surfaced that the original bids were between $6 and $6.50 over mean fob Med prices and the new bids may mean even higher premiums, some traders said.
Nov swaps ended at $226/$227, up from $224 on Wednesday but off its highs at $228/$229 as crude oil moved slightly lower. Dec rose $3.50 to $220.50.
Cargoes were notionally seen at $225/$227 cif NWE.
